Minimum wage indexed to inflation each September 30 from 2027 (Fla. Const. art. X, § 24(c)).

Minors: no Florida hour limits for 16-17 when school is not in session (federal has none either). The 16-17 30 h/week cap may be waived by a parent/custodian or the school superintendent on a state form.
Minors: § 450.081 does not apply to 16-17 graduates/GED holders, home-education or virtual-school students (16-17), or minors with a hardship waiver.
Minors: 15 and under may not work more than 4 hours continuously without a 30-minute meal period; 16-17 working 8+ hours likewise (§ 450.081(4)); not encoded (no minor-meal rule type).
Minors: FL 14-15 school-day 3 h cap does not apply when there is no school the next day (Friday); validator treats Mon-Fri as school days (stricter). Extra param key max_days_week.

X, § 24(c)): employers may credit tips 'up to the amount of the allowable FLSA tip credit in 2003'; the dollar amount is not stated in the constitution and FloridaCommerce could not be fetched, so no tipped_minimum_wage rule yet (tipped employees treated as owed the full $15.00 — conservative).

rules.summary: Florida's minimum wage is $15.00 an hour from September 30, 2026 (Fla. Const. art. X, § 24).

citation.title: Fla. Const. art. X, § 24(c) — Florida minimum wage
citation.excerpt: increase each September 30th thereafter by $1.00 per hour, until the Minimum Wage reaches $15.00 per hour on September 30th, 2026

rules.summary: While school is in session, minors 15 and under may work at most 3 hours on a school day (unless no school the next day) and 15 hours a week, not before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. before a school day.

citation.title: Fla. Stat. § 450.081 — Hours of work in certain occupations (2026)
citation.excerpt: Before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when school is scheduled the following day. 2. For more than 15 hours in any one week when school is in session ... may not be gainfully employed for more than 3 hours

rules.summary: During holidays and summer vacation, minors 15 and under may work at most 8 hours a day and 40 a week, between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m., and no more than 6 consecutive days.

citation.title: Fla. Stat. § 450.081 — Hours of work in certain occupations (2026)
citation.excerpt: During holidays and summer vacations, minors 15 years of age or younger may not be employed ... before 7 a.m. or after 9 p.m., for more than 8 hours in any one day, or for more than 40 hours

rules.summary: While school is in session, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 8 hours on a day before a school day (except holidays/Sundays) and 30 hours a week (waivable by parent or school), 6:30 a.m.-11 p.m. before a school day, and not during school hours.

citation.title: Fla. Stat. § 450.081 — Hours of work in certain occupations (2026)
citation.excerpt: Before 6:30 a.m. or after 11 p.m. when school is scheduled the following day. 2. For more than 8 hours in any one day when school is scheduled the following day ... 3. For more than 30 hours
